title: Adaptive autoscale and prioritized queueing for embedding & rerank endpoints
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Embeddings and reranking traffic exhibits bursty patterns (ad-hoc bulk ingest + interactive queries). Current fixed-instance pools lead to long queue latencies and costly overprovisioning. Goal: reduce p99 end-to-end latency for embeddings and rerank requests while improving cost-efficiency via adaptive autoscaling, prioritized queueing, and smarter rate limit behavior. This ticket covers design, prototype, instrumentation, and a staged rollout of an autoscaler and multi-queue adapter for the embeddings service.
acceptance_criteria: p99 enqueue-to-response latency <= 350ms for interactive traffic (batch size <= 64, seq <= 512) under median burst patterns observed in last 90 days
Autoscaler reduces idle GPU minutes by >= 20% on non-peak days compared to static pool baseline
No more than 0.5% of requests receive unexpected 5xx errors introduced by the new queueing layer during pilot
Thermostat SLO: graceful degradation path returns 202+queue-id for bulk jobs and 429 for interactive requests only when configured thresholds are exceeded
Instrumentation added: per-tenant queue depth, per-priority queue wait time, per-gpu batch utilization exposed to console

decision_log: Use two-tier queues: priority=interactive and priority=bulk. Interactive requests get bounded low-latency queues; bulk requests are accepted into a larger deferred queue and receive 202 with a queue-id.
Autoscaler strategy: combine short-term reactive scale-up (CPU/GPU headroom triggers) with ML-based 5-minute forecast warmups to reduce scale-up cold-starts.
Batching policy: token-aware keys with maximum batch size 128 for embeddings, prefer smaller batches for rerank to limit latency variance.
Backpressure semantics: 429 returned when interactive queue length > Q_int_high OR when global system GPU utilization > 95% and fallback budget exhausted.
Soft reservations: reserve a small fraction of GPU capacity per-tenant for SLO-critical customers (configurable).
metrics_target: p95 latency <= 200ms for interactive embed requests (seq<=512), p99 <= 350ms; bulk accepted-then-queued rate >= 99% under daily bursts; GPU batch_fill_ratio >= 0.7 during steady state
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated deploy to sandbox environment + replay historical traces (Week 1)
Pilot: enable for 5 low-risk customers in us-west (Week 2)
Monitor metrics for 72h, validate no increase in 5xx > 0.5% and cost improvements observed (Week 3)
Gradual ramp: increase to 25 customers and then regionally expand with canarying (Week 4+)
Post-mortem and tuning: collect telemetry and tune autoscaler thresholds, queue eviction policy (Post rollout)
Enterprise opt-out: ensure Dedicated customers can disable autoscaler and use pinned capacity per contract
notes: Trade-offs: returning 202 for bulk improves interactive latency but shifts complexity to clients to poll status. We'll provide SDK helpers to hide polling complexity.
Cost impact: predictive warmup increases short-term GPU minutes slightly but reduces cold-start latency and total overprovisioning. Target is net -20% idle minutes.
Open risks: inaccurate traffic forecast could cause flip-flop scaling. Mitigation: add smoothing windows and minimum up/down cooldowns.
Future: explore tenant-aware placement to colocate hot tenants on warm GPUs and use qsplitting for heterogeneous batch mixes.
